model: Recurring underlying profit capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR (-1.4%) diverges >30% from revenue 5y CAGR (+3.8%). Book equity is driven by investment-property revaluations (cumulative attributable fair-value losses of ~HK$28.6bn FY2020-25) and by dividends exceeding underlying profit, not by operating growth. Statutory EPS is negative in FY2024-25, so EPS CAGRs are not meaningful; reported FCF FY2022 was negative (-2,531), so the 3y FCF CAGR is not meaningful.
historical_growth.notes: The flow actually capitalised -- recurring underlying profit -- fell from HK$7,176m (FY2022) to HK$6,260m (FY2025), mainly from higher net finance cost as net debt rose from HK$18.9bn to HK$39.5bn to fund the HK$100bn plan, plus HK office rent reversion (HK office gross rental income -4% in FY2025). H1 FY2026 recurring UP rose 36% to HK$4,661m, largely on one-off trading sales. No SBC, so owner FCF and reported FCF differ only by the maintenance-capex treatment.

scenario_narratives.base: Ex-growth to 2027 as HK office reversion and plan-related interest offset the HK retail recovery; committed Mainland projects lift recurring profit ~4%/yr from 2028; capitalised at an 8% HKD cost of equity with net debt already serviced inside the flow.
scenario_narratives.bull: Office trough passes, HK retail and Mainland malls keep outperforming, trading book realises steadily; ~6%/yr recurring growth to FY2029 and a 7.5% cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural HK and Mainland office oversupply, thinner trading profits and rising finance costs leave recurring profit flat for four years; 9% cost of equity and a 12x exit cap.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Swire Properties is valued as what it is economically: a landlord whose distributable, post-interest, post-tax recurring profit accrues to equity holders. That stream is capitalised at an 8% HKD cost of equity with net debt held at zero (the debt is already serviced inside the flow). Revaluation gains and losses, and one-off divestment profits, are excluded. The result is deliberately an earnings value, not an appraisal NAV: book NAV of HK$47.08/share rests on 2.6-5.5% HK cap rates that no equity investor can earn, which is why the market prices the stock at ~0.5x book. The gap between this model and NAV is the value of being able to sell assets at appraisal (capital recycling), which the model does not credit.
key_risks_to_valuation: HK office rental reversion: Taikoo Place and Pacific Place offices are ~40% of gross rental income and face record Grade-A vacancy.
Chinese Mainland exposure (~40% of rents) to office oversupply and consumer weakness; the HK$100bn plan concentrates HK$46bn of commitments there.
Chinese Mainland retail lease-expiry concentration: ~31% of attributable Mainland retail gross rental income expires in 2026, into cautious tenant demand.
Rising net finance costs as the plan is debt-funded before new projects produce rent.
Trading profits are lumpy; the FY2026 base year normalises them, but a weak HK luxury residential market would undershoot.

Upside risk not in the model: continued capital recycling at or near appraisal values (e.g. Brickell City Centre, FY2025 divestment gains HK$2.36bn) realises NAV that the capitalisation approach ignores.
Dividend (HK$1.15 FY2025, 5% progressive growth) already exceeds recurring underlying EPS; sustaining it relies on divestment gains or rising gearing.
Partial offset in the base case: average cost of debt fell to 3.5% in FY2025 from 4.0%, which slows the finance-cost drag on the post-interest stream.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 19.90-27.18.
data_sources.financials: 1972.HK_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2017-H1 FY2026); FY2025 Annual Report ten-year summary, segment revenue/profit and IP valuation note 16; H1 FY2026 Interim Report highlights, underlying-profit reconciliation (p.17), capital commitments and net debt.
data_sources.qualitative: 1972.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-17): competitive position, risks, guidance (progressive mid-single-digit DPS growth, ~70% of HK$100bn plan committed) and bull/bear cases; plus chairman's/CEO statements in the FY2025 annual and H1 FY2026 interim.

inputs.sbc_source: Genuinely zero: FY2025 Annual Report states the Company has not adopted any share option scheme (1972.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:6250); EquityAwardTaxes 0 in every period.
inputs.share_count_basis: 5,757,484,800 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim note 11/25). No share option scheme, so basic = diluted. Held flat: the HK$738m buyback programme ran in FY2024-H1 FY2025 and nothing was repurchased in H1 FY2026.
inputs.flow_definition: The capitalised stream is Recurring Underlying Profit attributable to shareholders (company's audited non-GAAP measure, H1 FY2026 interim p.17 reconciliation): reported profit excluding investment-property fair-value movements and their deferred tax, and excluding profit from divestments. It is AFTER net finance costs, AFTER tax and AFTER NCI, and includes the attributable share of JV/associate profits (whose debt is therefore also already serviced). Engine mapping: base_revenue = FY2025 recurring underlying profit HK$6,260m; ebitda margin 100%; cash tax 0%; D&A 0%; capex_pct = maintenance/refurbishment capex on the investment portfolio, which recurring UP never charges because IP is carried at fair value and not depreciated.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: net_debt held at ZERO deliberately. The flow is post-interest, so deducting net debt as well would charge the debt twice. Actual balance-sheet anchors at 30 June 2026 for the record: total borrowings HK$49,221m (excl. leases), cash HK$9,424m, net debt incl. lease liabilities HK$40,268m (company definition), gearing 14.8%; attributable JV/associate net debt would lift gearing to 17.9%. The rising interest bill from debt-funding the HK$100bn plan is carried in the growth path (it is why recurring UP fell from 7,285 in FY2023 to 6,260 in FY2025).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the HKD COST OF EQUITY, not WACC, because the flow is to equity. HKD is pegged to USD: risk-free ~3.75% (blend of HK Exchange Fund 10y ~3.5% and UST 10y ~4.2%), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.85 for a low-geared (14.8%) landlord whose rental base is ~60% Hong Kong and ~40% Chinese Mainland -> 8.0% base. Bull 7.5% (Mainland retail stabilises, HK office trough passes), bear 9.0% (Mainland office oversupply and HK office vacancy persist). House precedent: 0004.HK Wharf capitalised UNP at 9.5% (Mainland-led, weaker portfolio); 1113.HK CK Asset at 8%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities (~HK$497m) are small; recurring UP already charges amortisation of right-of-use assets held as IP (reconciliation item f). No separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Recurring UP is attributable to the Company's shareholders, so NCI (HK$1,882m at FY2025) is already excluded from the flow. No bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md to the REIT / property-trust row (IAS 40 fair-value landlord): distributable-profit capitalisation at cost of equity, net debt held at zero. Swire Properties is internally managed and has a development arm, but ~90% of net assets employed are investment property (FY2025: IP 278,827 / trading 25,857 / hotels 6,198 of 310,882) and statutory profit is dominated by revaluation noise (FY2025 reported loss HK$1,533m after HK$8,002m attributable fair-value losses vs underlying profit HK$8,620m), so an owner-FCF DCF on reported earnings/FCF is meaningless here. Same family as 0004.HK (UNP at CoE). Trading profit is lumpy (FY2017-25 average ~HK$200m; H1 FY2026 HK$1,211m on two 6 Deep Water Bay Road houses), so the year-1 step normalises it to ~HK$800m/yr against a HK$25.9bn trading book rather than annualising H1 FY2026 recurring UP of HK$4,661m. Divestment gains (HK$2,360m FY2025) are excluded as non-recurring: they are the realisation of appraisal value, which this model does not credit -- see NAV cross-check. NAV CROSS-CHECK: equity attributable per share HK$47.08 at 30 June 2026 with completed HK investment property valued at 2.63-5.50% cap rates and Mainland at 5.50-6.50% (FY2025 AR note 16); the price is ~0.52x that book NAV. Capitalising the same rents at an 8% cost of equity is precisely why this model lands far below book NAV: the appraisal cap rates sit below any plausible equity return. Hotels (HK$6.2bn net assets, ~zero underlying profit) receive no value in this model -- a deliberate conservatism worth ~HK$1/share at book. Qualitative context: 1972.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-17) was read after the first build and is consistent with the driver paths (office oversupply HK + Mainland, retail momentum, cost of debt down to 3.5% in FY2025, ~31% of Mainland retail rent expiring in 2026); no driver was changed as a result.

bear.narrative: HK Grade-A office vacancy stays high and Taikoo Place/Pacific Place rents reset lower at expiry; Mainland office oversupply (Shanghai, Guangzhou, Beijing all flagged in the FY2025 outlook) spreads into retail; trading profits shrink to ~HK$0.3bn; and rising net debt for the plan pushes finance costs up faster than new rent arrives. Recurring UP stalls near HK$6.4-6.5bn for four years; cost of equity 9%.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2026 +10% to ~HK$6.9bn normalises: property investment ~HK$6.1bn (H1 3,445 annualised, less a softer H2 as Brickell rent is fully gone), trading ~HK$0.8bn normalised (not the H1 HK$1.2bn one-off), hotels ~0. FY2027 +3%: HK retail recovery offset by HK office reversion and the interest cost of the plan. FY2028-30 +4%: committed Mainland projects (Taikoo Li Xi'an, Qiantan, Julong Wan Guangzhou, Lujiazui Taikoo Yuan, Taikoo Hui Phase 3) open and the HK residential pipeline realises. Then fades to 2.5%.
base.capex_pct_note: Maintenance/refurbishment of the completed portfolio at ~8% of the stream (~HK$550m, ~4% of HK$13.0bn gross rental income). Growth capex for the HK$100bn plan is NOT charged and its incremental rent is credited only through the modest growth path -- i.e. the plan is treated as roughly NPV-neutral at the cost of equity (6-7% Mainland yield on cost, ~25% tax, ~4% debt funding).
base.wacc_note: Cost of equity, not WACC: the stream is post-interest.
base.narrative: Swire Properties remains a high-quality but ex-growth landlord through 2027: HK retail recovers on tourism and luxury demand while HK office rents keep reverting under record vacancy, and the interest cost of the HK$100bn plan absorbs most of the rental growth. From 2028 the committed Mainland retail-led projects lift recurring profit ~4% a year before fading to inflation-like growth.

bull.narrative: HK office occupancy recovers on the IPO and financial-services rebound, HK retail extends its H1 FY2026 momentum, trading realises ~HK$1.2bn/yr from the HK$25.9bn book, and Mainland retail openings land ahead of schedule. Recurring UP reaches ~HK$7.3bn in FY2026 and compounds ~6% to FY2029; risk premium compresses to 7.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: HK office (~40% of gross rental income) faces record vacancy and new supply, the Chinese Mainland office market is explicitly guided weaker for 2026, and recurring profit has fallen three years running. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs office, Mainland retail and the trading book to all turn together, although H1 FY2026 retail momentum is real. Balance sheet risk is low (14.8% gearing), so no solvency tail is weighted.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
